extracted.intended_audience: Employees of the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), including career staff, SES, political appointees, procurement officials, and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of ethics rules and standards governing USPTO employees' conduct, including conflicts of interest, gifts, misuse of resources, outside employment, political activity, seeking/post-employment restrictions, financial disclosure, and training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service is a public trust (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service is a public trust, requiring employees to place loyalty to the Constitution, the laws and ethical principles above private gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must familiarize themselves with Government ethics rules and comply with applicable restrictions while performing duties and, in some cases, during personal activities off duty and after leaving Federal service. Seek advice from ethics officials for specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid financial interests that conflict with duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not hold financial interests that conflict with the conscientious performance of duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicting financial interests require disqualification from matters affecting those interests; see financial-conflict thresholds and disqualification rules later in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on trading on nonpublic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not engage in financial transactions using nonpublic Government information or allow the improper use of such information to further any private interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpublic information includes privileged or insider information gained through employment; its use for personal investment or benefit is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift acceptance restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee shall not, except as permitted in ethics regulations, solicit or accept any gift or other item of monetary value from any person or entity seeking official action from, doing business with, or conducting activities regulated by the employee’s agency, or whose interests may be substantially affected by the performance or non-performance of the employee’s duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Gifts and Bribes section for permitted exceptions (e.g., small unsolicited gifts, certain invitations) and prohibited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest effort in performance of duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall put forth honest effort in the performance of their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unauthorized commitments or promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not knowingly make unauthorized commitments or promises of any kind purporting to bind the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use public office for private gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not use public office for private gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes misuse of title, authority, or nonpublic information to benefit oneself or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act impartially and avoid preferential treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall act impartially and not give preferential treatment to any private organization or individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be made without favoritism; apparent bias should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and conserve Federal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall protect and conserve Federal property and shall not use it for other than authorized activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government titles, equipment, services, supplies and nonpublic information are considered public property and must be used only as authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid outside employment that conflicts with duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall not engage in outside employment or activities, including seeking or negotiating for employment, that conflict with official Government duties and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Non-Federal Employment and Activities and Seeking Employment sections for permitted/prohibited activities and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall disclose waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption to appropriate authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report to Office of Inspector General or other proper authorities; Ethics Division advises but does not investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfy obligations as citizens (including taxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall satisfy in good faith their obligations as citizens, including all just financial obligations, especially those–such as Federal, State, or local taxes–that are imposed by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to equal opportunity laws and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall adhere to all laws and regulations that provide equal opportunity for all Americans regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, or handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid actions creating appearance of impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees shall endeavor to avoid any actions creating the appearance that they are violating the law or the ethical standards set forth in ethics regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an appearance exists is determined from the perspective of a reasonable person with knowledge of the relevant facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misuse of Government resources (Basic Principle: Do Not Steal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government equipment, services, supplies, titles, nonpublic information, and time are public property and must be used only for Government purposes or authorized personal uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses include limited personal email/internet use that does not interfere with work and is not for commercial, partisan, or otherwise prohibited purposes; permitted use of Government title for biographical info or scientific publications with disclaimers; use of frequent-flyer miles earned on Government travel for personal purposes. Prohibited uses include using Government credit cards for personal purchases (except authorized), viewing sexually explicit material, running a business, political activity using Government resources, using nonpublic information for investment, using Government time for personal activities, or using Government authority to benefit oneself or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and bribes — general principle (Avoid undue influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are separate rules for personal gifts from non-Government sources, gifts from other Federal employees, and gifts/donations to the agency; criminal statutes bar accepting a bribe or salary supplementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bribe is anything of value offered to take action (or fail to take action) as a Government employee; different statutory provisions govern types of gifts and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal gifts from non-Government sources — permitted categories
rubrics_metrics.description: You can accept an unsolicited gift or invitation if it is: offered by someone with no business before Commerce and not offered because of your Government position; from a relative or friend; $20 or less in value (and you received $50 or less in gifts from the same source during the year); an invitation to a widely-attended gathering with supervisor approval; a meal at which you are speaking in an official capacity; a discount available to the public or all Federal employees; offered because of your spouse’s employment; a card/plaque/other item of little intrinsic value; an approved award; certain business-meal or travel exceptions; from a foreign government valued at $375 or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some exceptions do not apply to political appointees when the donor is a registered lobbyist or lobbying organization (with certain exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal gifts from non-Government sources — prohibited acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot accept a gift or invitation if it is offered by someone that is regulated by Commerce, has or seeks business with Commerce, or can be affected by the performance of your duties (unless listed as permitted); if it is offered because of your Government position (unless permitted); or if it is specifically to take action (or fail to take action) as a Government employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal gifts from other Federal employees — permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: You can accept a gift or invitation from another Federal employee if it is not from a subordinate; $10 or less in value; for a special major event (birth, retirement, serious illness, wedding); food shared in the office; personal hospitality at the employee’s home; or a host/hostess gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can offer such permitted gifts to a supervisor if they meet the listed criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal gifts from other Federal employees — prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot accept a gift or invitation from another Federal employee if it is offered by a subordinate, unless it falls within permitted exceptions (<= $10, major life event, shared food, host/hostess gift). You cannot offer a gift to a supervisor unless listed as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts/donations to the USPTO — permitted agency acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may accept a gift or donation of property or travel if it will further a Government program, is approved by the appropriate agency official, and acceptance will not create an appearance of loss of impartiality (donor generally not on prohibited list). Travel payment can be accepted from local/regional IP associations for dissemination of information if traveler is not policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance requires agency approval and consideration of appearance-of-impartiality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts/donations to the USPTO — prohibited agency acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO cannot accept gifts or donations if they are for services (unless travel), will not further an agency mission, create appearance of undue influence (e.g., from contractors, likely patent seekers, patent practitioners/organizations, or controversial donors), or if for Government travel that was solicited or is for first-class travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and disqualifications — basic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees have conflicts of interest when personal interests (or those of close persons) differ from Government interests; ethics laws require disqualification from working on matters in which there are such conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts can arise from financial interests, outside positions, or personal relationships; disqualification rules explained in financial and personal-relationship subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflicts of interest — permitted actions (no conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can work on matters affecting a financial interest in: a stock or bond valued at $15,000 or less; a broadly-diversified mutual fund; a sector-specific fund valued at $50,000 or less; interests held by an adult child (if not living in your household); or interests covered by a conflict waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds apply only to securities traded on a U.S. exchange unless otherwise noted; see prohibited-actions thresholds for higher-value holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflicts of interest — prohibited actions (disqualification required)
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot work on a matter if agency action will affect: a company in which you hold stock greater than $15,000 (with higher thresholds for certain sector/policy matters), stock totaling greater than $50,000 in companies affected by the matter, interests in sector-specific funds greater than $50,000, non-exchange-traded interests (real estate, partnerships, foreign securities, options, patent rights), or a company/organization with which you are employed, serve as officer, or serve on a governing board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualification required when the financial interest meets prohibiting thresholds; includes interests held by spouse, minor child, household member, or general partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited disqualification for some financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: You may participate in general policy matters, but not in matters involving specific parties, that will affect companies in which you hold stock valued at $15,001–$25,000, financial interests of household members (not spouse/minor child), or interests covered by a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a partial participation rule: full disqualification may not be required for broad policy matters but is required for matters involving specific parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest based on personal relationships — permitted actions
rubrics_metrics.description: You can work on a matter involving a party (or its representative) with whom you have a personal relationship if the relationship concerns a close friend; a former employer or client you worked for more than one year ago (career) or more than two years before appointment (political appointees); an organization in which you are a member but not active; someone with whom your business dealings are limited to routine consumer transactions; or if you have received special authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special authorization to work on a matter despite a close personal/business relationship must be obtained through the Ethics Law and Programs Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest based on personal relationships — prohibited actions
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot work on a matter involving a party (or its representative) with whom you have a business or financial relationship; a close relative; an organization in which you are active; the employer or client (or prospective employer/client) of your parents, spouse, or dependent child; someone with whom you were employed or served as agent/attorney/consultant/contractor/director/general partner/trustee during the past year; or (for political appointees) someone with whom you had such relationships during the two years before appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such relationships create conflicts requiring disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on investments and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If disqualification due to a financial interest or outside employment would prevent performance of important duties, you should not make the investment or engage in the activity. You also cannot obtain an interest in a patent (other than by inheritance), use nonpublic information from Federal employment to make investment decisions, or (if filing OGE Form 278) invest in an IPO except in same manner as available to the public generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid investments or activities that will create unavoidable conflicts; follow special IPO and patent-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Federal employment and activities — permitted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Work outside USPTO is permitted if it will not impair Government duties, create appearance of using office for private gain, and is not expressly prohibited. You can work for anyone who does not have matters before your office (unless otherwise prohibited), teach and write for pay if subject is not related to Commerce programs/policies, teach/write about Commerce without pay (with agency review in some cases), contact a Federal agency on behalf of certain close family members with prior approval, practice law as a personal activity if you do not represent clients before a Federal agency or court or advise on matters where the U.S. is a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior approvals and restrictions apply for some employees (noncareer SES member approval for paid teaching on Commerce subjects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Federal employment and activities — prohibited activities
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot be employed by or hold a position with a foreign government; contact a Federal agency or court on behalf of someone else (except narrow exceptions); be employed by someone whose financial interests can be affected by your duties (unless duties can be reassigned); hold office or board membership in an organization whose financial interests can be affected by your duties (unless duties reassigned); be paid for teaching/speaking/writing about Commerce programs unless teaching is part of regular academic curriculum; noncareer SES members face limits on outside earned income and fiduciary affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activities — overarching principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mix politics and public service: restrictions protect objectivity of Government operations and insulating employees from undue political influence while preserving employees' rights as private citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal law imposes restrictions tailored to on-duty/off-duty status and employee category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activities — permitted activities (all employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees can give funds to a candidate or party; attend a political fundraiser, rally, or campaign event; vote; sign political petitions; display political bumper stickers on personal cars or wear political buttons when not on duty and not on Federal premises; put a political sign on their lawn; and run for office in a non-partisan election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees who are not career SES members have additional permitted activities (assist in campaign management, serve as officer in political group, make phone calls/solicit votes but not funds, stuff envelopes, speak at events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activities — prohibited activities (all employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees cannot engage in political activities while on Government premises or duty; use Government resources (including agency title or email/internet) for political activities; ask for or accept political contributions; host a political fundraiser; use Government authority to support/oppose a partisan candidate or party; run as a candidate in a partisan election (with narrow local exceptions); ask for/accept volunteer services from a subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career SES members face stricter prohibitions (cannot assist campaigns even off-duty or hold office in a political organization). Some exceptions apply to Presidential appointees in Senate-confirmed positions regarding on-premises activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking employment outside the Government — restrictions during job search
rubrics_metrics.description: You are free to look for career opportunities outside the Government but cannot work as a Federal employee on any matter that would affect anyone you have contacted about possible future employment or who has contacted you about such employment, until discussions end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice requirements: SES, SL/ST, political appointees, or others required to file OGE Form 278 must notify an ethics official within three days of an employment contact that they will not participate in matters affecting the prospective employer; procurement officials with procurements $100,000+ must notify supervisor and ethics official of employment contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restrictions — all employees (permitted activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: After leaving Federal service you can engage in activities that do not involve representing others before the Federal Government; represent others on matters you did not participate in and were not under your responsibility during your last year (unless senior employee restrictions apply); represent others before the Federal Government on matters that do not involve specific parties (unless senior restrictions apply); represent the District of Columbia or, as an elected official, a state/local government before the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restrictions — all employees (prohibited activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: After leaving Federal service you cannot represent others before a Federal agency or court regarding a specific-party matter on which you worked; represent others before a Federal agency or court within two years of leaving USPTO regarding a specific-party matter that was under your official responsibility during your last year; disclose or use nonpublic information; receive compensation for others' representational activities before the Government during the period you worked for USPTO; represent others or assist others regarding representation before USPTO for two years regarding a patent application on which you worked or which was under your responsibility; or apply for a patent or obtain rights to a patent for one year after leaving USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional restrictions apply for senior employees, political appointees, procurement officials, and attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restrictions — additional restrictions for senior employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior employees (base pay $158,554.50 or more) may, in addition to permitted activities for all employees, represent certain educational/medical research institutions before USPTO on non-specific-party matters; but within one year after leaving they cannot represent others before USPTO (or Department for Under Secretary), represent a foreign government before any U.S. Government branch, or assist/advice a foreign government regarding dealings with the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restrictions — additional restrictions for political appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: Political appointees may represent higher-education/hospital/medical research institutions before USPTO on non-specific-party matters (as above) but cannot, for the remainder of the President's term, serve as a lobbyist before any Executive Branch political appointee; and if a senior employee, for two years cannot represent others before USPTO (or Department for Under Secretary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restrictions — procurement officials and attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement officials/program managers cannot accept compensation from a contractor of a procurement of $10,000,000 or more within one year of working on the procurement. Attorneys must comply with bar rules, which may prohibit certain behind-the-scenes legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional position-specific restrictions may apply; see Ethics Law and Programs Division for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure requirements — OGE Form 450 filers (procurement and public-affect duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement officials and other employees with duties that could affect the public who are designated as OGE Form 450 filers must file a new entrant OGE Form 450 within 30 days of entering the position and file an annual OGE Form 450 every year on February 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available on the Ethics Law and Programs Division website; human resources can advise on filing requirements. Ethics training: attend an ethics briefing once every three years and review materials in intervening years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure requirements — OGE Form 278 filers (SES, SL/ST, political appointees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Senior Executive Service, SL/ST employees, and political appointees who file OGE Form 278 must file a new entrant OGE Form 278 within 30 days of appointment; an annual OGE Form 278 every year by May 15; a termination OGE Form 278 within 30 days after leaving Federal service; an OGE Form 278-T Transaction Report within 30 days of a transaction regarding a security > $1,000; and a Notice of Employment Negotiation within 3 business days of an employment contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and filing instructions are available on the Ethics Law and Programs Division website. Ethics training: required every year for these filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees are required to receive ethics training: OGE Form 450 filers must attend an ethics briefing once every three years and review ethics materials in other years; members of SES, SL/ST, and political appointees (OGE Form 278 filers) are required to receive ethics training every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training materials and briefings are provided by the Ethics Law and Programs Division; keep records and comply with frequency and content requirements.
